questions.question: What are scope, hoisting, and the temporal dead zone in JavaScript?
questions.title: Scope Hoisting Tdz
questions.direct_answer: Scope: where a variable is visible. Hoisting: declarations are processed before code runs (var initialized to undefined; let/const known but unusable). TDZ: the zone between a block's start and a let/const declaration line where accessing the variable throws.

sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: Scope: where a variable is visible. Hoisting: declarations are processed before code runs (var initialized to undefined; let/const known but unusable). TDZ: the zone between a block's start and a let/const declaration line where accessing the variable throws.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C[compile scope] --> R[register declarations]
    R -->|var| INIT[initialize to undefined — usable]
    R -->|let/const| TDZ[NO initialization — TDZ]
    TDZ -->|access before declaration| ERR[ReferenceError]
    INIT →|access before declaration| UNDEF[undefined — silent]
    L[declaration line] -->|let/const| OK[initialized — usable]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The compilation model, mechanically: the engine parses and compiles each scope (function, block) — during this, it registers ALL declarations in the scope's environment. var declarations are registered AND initialized (to undefined) — the binding exists with a value. let/const are registered but NOT initialized — the binding exists in the environment with no value, which IS the TDZ state.

The block-scoping mechanics: each block ({}) that contains let/const gets its own lexical environment (a chained scope). The TDZ is that environment's entry minus the declaration line's initialization. This is why a block can shadow an outer variable without touching it: the block's environment has its own binding, and until the declaration, that binding is in the TDZ.

The function hoisting asymmetry (the follow-up): function DECLARATIONS are hoisted completely (identifier + body) — calling a function before its declaration works. Function EXPRESSIONS (const f = () => {}) hoist only per their let/const rules (TDZ). This is why 'can I call this before I define it?' depends on the syntax used.
